names.name: Riviera
names.note: Opened 1931 in Fort Lee; first building burned Thanksgiving 1936; rebuilt 1937; closed in early WWII

names.name: Bill Miller's Riviera
names.note: Reopened by Miller (his page says bought 1945); closed 4 Oct 1953 for the Palisades Parkway; demolished 1954

label.basis: The pages opened give no organized-crime claim for the Riviera either way; no primary source was opened.

venues.corrections: Opening year is 1931 (Ben Marden), not 1930. The name 'Bill Miller's Riviera' applies only from 1946 (1945 per Miller's page); closed 1953 is confirmed. The 'alleged' label could not be sourced.

names.name: 500 Cafe
names.note: Built by Barr in the mid-1930s as a betting parlor and nightclub; repossessed and closed for a time; D'Amato investors took over

names.name: 500 Club
names.operator: Paul 'Skinny' D'Amato (with Irvin Wolf, then sole owner by 1949)
names.note: Renamed when D'Amato and Wolf bought out the half-interest in June 1946; burned in an electrical fire in June 1973

label.basis: 1950 Kefauver testimony names D'Amato as manager and Reginelli as county racket boss, and Wikipedia says D'Amato had mob ties, but no opened source shows a conviction, a court finding or Bruno control of the club.

venues.corrections: Opening is mid-1930s (500 Cafe, Phil Barr), not firmly 1930. The 'documented' label is not supported by what was opened: the Kefauver hearings of 1950 contain witness statements, not a finding of Bruno family control (Bruno led after 1959), D'Amato was never convicted, and the NJ Crime Commission was not opened. Suggest 'alleged'.

names.name: Club Harlem
names.operator: Leroy "Pop" Williams, later with Clifton Williams and Ben Alten
names.note: On the site of Fitzgerald's Auditorium; closed 1986; demolished 1992

label.basis: Only a Wikipedia history was read, and it shows no mob ownership; a 1972 Black Mafia shootout occurred in the club but concerns violence, not ownership.

names.name: Chalfonte-Haddon Hall
names.note: Hotel complex returned to owners 1946; Resorts bought Leeds & Lippincott 1976

names.name: Resorts International Hotel Casino
names.operator: Resorts International (Mary Carter Paint origin); James Crosby; Trump held control 1987-88
names.note: Opened 26 May 1978; Merv Griffin took the company Nov 1988

names.name: Resorts Casino Hotel
names.operator: Griffin Gaming; Sun International; Colony Capital; lenders 2009; later owners
names.note: Sold in turn; lenders took the property in 2009

label.basis: Only a CIA-front reputation for Mary Carter is on the pages opened; no opened source states a Lansky link.

venues.corrections: The Lansky link in the current summary is not stated by any source opened (the Resorts International page says Mary Carter was widely considered a CIA front).

names.name: Bally's Atlantic City
names.operator: Bally Manufacturing successors; Harrah's (2005); Vici (2017); Twin River/Bally's Corp. (2020)

label.basis: The NJCCC history says Bally's executives were found unsuitable and removed, and Wikipedia says Bally's head resigned over alleged organized crime links, which he denied.

venues.corrections: The 'none' label is contradicted: the NJCCC history records executives found unsuitable at Bally's licensing, and Wikipedia reports the head resigned over alleged mob links. The grounds were not read in a primary decision.

names.name: Boardwalk Regency
names.note: Opened 26 Jun 1979 on a temporary licence

names.name: Caesars Atlantic City
names.operator: Caesars World, ITT, Starwood, Park Place/Harrah's, Caesars Entertainment; Vici owns real estate (2017)

label.basis: The NJCCC found executives unsuitable and denied the Perlman brothers permanent licences over dealings with Malnik, identified as a Lansky associate.

venues.corrections: The 'Chicago Outfit' wording is not supported by any source opened: the dealings named are with Alvin Malnik (Lansky associate, Miami) and a Teamsters pension loan to Malnik/Cohen sons. Underlying court opinions were not opened.

names.name: Holiday Inn Marina Casino (planned)
names.operator: LM Walters Co and Holiday Inns

names.name: Harrah's Marina Hotel Casino
names.operator: Holiday Inns; later Harrah's Entertainment/Caesars; Vici real estate (2020)

label.basis: The page opened gives no organized-crime link, and I found no sceptical or supporting source.

names.name: Ambassador Hotel
names.note: Old hotel on the site; reported site of the 1929 gangster conference

label.basis: No opened source ties the casino to organized crime; the 1929 conference concerns the earlier hotel.

names.name: Trump Plaza
names.operator: Trump (bought out Harrah's 1986); Trump Hotels & Casino Resorts (1995)
names.note: Closed 16 Sep 2014; Icahn took the land

label.basis: No opened source links Trump Plaza to organized-crime contractors; the Scarfo page only says his cement firm worked on Atlantic City casinos in general.

venues.corrections: The concrete-contractor claim is not supported by any source opened, and the Trump Plaza page does not mention it.

names.name: Trump Taj Mahal
names.operator: Donald Trump; Trump Hotels & Casino Resorts (1996); Icahn (2016)

names.name: Hard Rock Hotel & Casino Atlantic City
names.operator: Hard Rock International (Seminole Tribe) with Morris and Jingoli families

label.basis: Wikipedia reports a 1992 Senate subcommittee report naming an executive as a triad associate and Russian mobsters among patrons; the report itself was not opened.

venues.corrections: The concrete-contractor claim is not supported by any source opened. The reported ties are an employee named in a 1992 Senate report and Russian mob patrons. Ownership by the mob is not claimed.

names.name: Borgata
names.operator: MGM Mirage and Boyd Gaming; MGM Resorts (2016); Vici (2022 via MGM Growth)
names.note: Opened 2 Jul 2003; MGM sold its stake in 2010 settlement

label.basis: The page opened shows no organized-crime tie at the Borgata itself.

gaps: Resorts: Lansky-link claims were not fetched (Miami Beach police study, UPI and company-histories hosts blocked).
500 Club: NJ State Commission of Investigation reports and the Kefauver final report were not opened (hosts blocked); Kefauver Part 18 and Part 11 searched via archive.org text.
Caesars, Bally's: NJCCC decisions and In re Boardwalk Regency (90 N.J. 361) not opened: justia is behind a Cloudflare challenge, leagle, courtlistener and dspace.njstatelib.org blocked.
Trump Plaza and Taj: DGE 1987 report and 1992 Senate report not opened (archive.org PDF downloads failed); FinCEN penalties not opened.
Riviera (Fort Lee): no primary or contemporary source found; no mob claim verified. Harlem, Harrah's, Tropicana and Borgata checked on Wikipedia only.
Archive.org Kefauver parts 6-8 searched for Atlantic City with nothing relevant.
